## The trap

`child_process.execFileSync(file, args, opts)` (and `execSync`) **inherit the child's
stderr to the parent process by default** — Node's documented behavior: *"stderr by
default will be output to the parent process' stderr unless stdio is specified."*

So a best-effort git probe like:

```ts
execFileSync('git', ['-C', root, 'rev-list', '--count', 'main..staging'], { encoding: 'utf8' })
```

when it runs somewhere with **no `.git`** (a **packaged desktop install** — there is no
checkout — or a fresh/other dir) writes the raw, untagged

```
fatal: not a git repository (or any parent up to mount point /)
Stopping at filesystem boundary (GIT_DISCOVERY_ACROSS_FILESYSTEM not set).
```

straight to the process's own stderr → `serve.log`. Two lines **per call**. A boot-time
watchdog that fires several git calls at boot **and** on an interval turns this into
15+ lines of boot-log noise that buries real errors. `.catch(() => null)` does **not**
help — the child already wrote to fd 2 before the throw is caught.

This has now recurred twice (EI-8794, then EI-9922) across different boot components.

## The rule

For any git shell-out that is **best-effort** and **might run outside a git repo**
(version/sha detection, integration-root resolution, boot/health watchdogs), pin:

```ts
execFileSync('git', args, { encoding: 'utf8', stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'ignore'] })
```

`['ignore', 'pipe', 'ignore']` = ignore stdin, **capture** stdout (so you still get the
result), **discard** stderr. This is the established pattern in `build-info.ts`
(`defaultGitSha`), `desktop-install/workspace-map.ts`, and `endpoint-route/routes/desktop/version.ts`.

The async `execFile`/`spawn` (callback/promise) forms **buffer** stderr instead of
inheriting it, so they don't leak raw — but they can still log a scary line in a
`catch`. On a **not-a-repo** error specifically, that is the *expected* no-op state on a
packaged install, so **go quiet**: match the message (`/not a git repository/i`) and skip
the log; keep logging genuinely different git faults (auth, `git not found`).

## Regression-test shape

Mock `node:child_process` and assert the suppressing stdio is passed:

```ts
vi.mock('node:child_process', async (importOriginal) => {
  const actual = await importOriginal<typeof import('node:child_process')>();
  return { ...actual, execFileSync: vi.fn(actual.execFileSync) };
});
// ...
expect(vi.mocked(execFileSync)).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
  'git', expect.arrayContaining(['rev-list']),
  expect.objectContaining({ stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'ignore'] }),
);
```

For the async/quiet path, inject a `runGit` that throws a `not a git repository` error
and assert the `log` spy is **not** called.
